chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The boundary of the Garden in the Masjid of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) is up to the side of the shaded area, and the boundary of the Masjid is up to the two pillars from the right of the Pulpit up to the street from what follows the night market.

key_terms.الرَّوْضَةِ: The Garden (specifically referring to the Rawdah al-Mutaharramah in Medina)
key_terms.الظِّلَالِ: The shaded area (referring to the covered part of the mosque)
key_terms.سُوقَ اللَّيْلِ: The night market (a historical street name in Medina)
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ الرَّسُولِ: The Masjid of the Messenger (Prophet's Mosque)

ai.seo_question: What are the defined boundaries of the Rawdah and the Masjid in the Prophet's Mosque according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi precisely delineates the sacred boundaries of the Rawdah al-Sharifah and the Masjid al-Nabawi, anchoring the Rawdah's limit to the edge of the shade and the Masjid's extent to the two pillars near the Minbar. These specific landmarks are foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the ritual status of prayer and the sanctity of the site, reflecting the enduring reverence for the Prophet's physical presence. The description highlights the continuity of the mosque's layout from the time of the Prophet (saww) to the era of the Imams, preserving the spatial theology of the holy sanctuary.
